title: Characteristic ideal of the fine Selmer group and results on $Œº$-invariance under isogeny in the function field case

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: In the l≠p part, the paper repeatedly states that G=Gal(K∞/K) is pro-p. But K∞=K(E[ℓ∞]) and the Galois group is an open subgroup of GL2(Z_ℓ), hence not pro-p; the relevant pro-ℓ subgroup (or compact ℓ-adic Lie group) should be used instead.

predicted_errors.error_location: Definition 2.14 and its use in Section 6/Appendix A
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The μ-invariant is defined using p^i(M[p∞])/p^{i+1} and ord_p in Corollary 2.17, but in the ℓ≠p part the Selmer modules are ℓ-primary and the Iwasawa algebra is Z_ℓ[[G]]. As written, the μ-invariant would be trivially zero or undefined; the definition should use ℓ, not p.

predicted_errors.error_location: Theorem 5.1 statement in Section 5 vs. Theorem 1.6 and Remark 1.7
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The abstract/main theorem assumes H^2_fl(K∞,E_i[p∞])=0, but the later statement of Theorem 5.1 says H^1_fl(K∞,E_i[p∞])=0. These are contradictory hypotheses.

It states 'the order of the kernel of isogeny equals its separable degree.' In positive characteristic this is false: the order of the kernel equals the degree of the isogeny, while the separable degree is the number of geometric points. For Frobenius, the degree is q but the separable degree is 1.

It claims a Λ-isomorphism from T_p M^S(E/L_n) to a direct sum of Λ/Φ_{c_i}. But T_p M^S(E/L_n) is a Z_p-module of finite rank, while the right side is a torsion Λ-module; such an isomorphism cannot exist as stated.
The characteristic ideal formula is over n≥0 with e_n=(rank E(L_n)-rank E(L_{n-1}))/φ(p^n). For n=0, L_{-1} is undefined. In Remark 3.6, the same e_n is defined only for n≥1.

predicted_errors.error_location: Proof of Theorem 5.1, local argument after equation (10)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper says 'for any prime v and w|v, Gal(K_{\infty,w}/K_{\infty,w}) ≅ ∏_{ℓ≠p} Z_ℓ.' The Galois group of a field over itself is trivial. Moreover, the arithmetic Z_p-extension has local Galois group Z_p, not the prime-to-p product.
The second inequality is stated as |H^1(G,B)| ≤ |B|^{d(d-1)/2}, but the exponent d(d-1)/2 is the standard bound for H^2(G,B), not H^1(G,B).

For the map g₂ between H^1(G_S(K_cyc), E₁[ℓ∞]) and H^1(G_S(K_cyc), E₂[ℓ∞]), the proof claims coker(g₂)=H¹(G_S(K), A). The long exact sequence over K_cyc identifies the cokernel as a subquotient of H²(K_cyc,A), not with H¹(G_S(K),A).
The recursive definition of the Carlitz polynomial is garbled: it lists '1 = X', 't = X^p + tX', 't^n = t)' and a self-referential formula. A rigorous definition requires notation such as [P(t)](X).

Both entries refer to the same paper: Coates, Schneider, Sujatha, 'Links between cyclotomic and GL₂ Iwasawa theory', Doc. Math. Extra Vol. 2003, pages 187–215. The duplicate citation should be consolidated.
The proposition statement gives only part (a), but the proof explicitly proves '(a) and (b)' and later says 'Then, (b) follows'. A part (b) is missing from the statement.
